reason: E2 directly supports that 0.1 at.% B in an equimolar BCC RHEA induces intergranular boride precipitation, enhances grain boundary cohesion, and improves ductility. However, E1 concerns a different alloy system (Al-Nb-Ta-Ti-V-Zr) and a phase-inversion strategy, not boron addition, so it does not support the specific premises about boron's effect. The premises about high-temperature strength retention and irradiation tolerance are not addressed by the cited evidence.
premises: Boron addition enhances grain boundary cohesion in refractory high-entropy alloys
Intergranular boride precipitates form with ~0.1 at.% B in BCC RHEAs
Enhanced grain boundary cohesion improves room-temperature ductility
BCC matrix retains high-temperature strength after minor B addition
Boron-modified RHEAs maintain or improve irradiation tolerance
